title: feat(spec): enable.aiReadable — a system object's author can open its records to the AI read tools, read-only
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D6CXpVXQSJdtd7DyYBcaVe3)_

Fixes #32865

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: added
Skills-docs: follow-up #32974 — skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md (the `enable` capability table has no `aiReadable` row; it should say the key is refused on any object whose name does not start with `sys_`, so an app author never writes it)

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：对象的 `enable` 块新增 `aiReadable`（只读的 AI 开放声明）。只有系统表（`sys_` 开头）可以声明，声明后 AI 的读工具（查询、取单条、聚合、描述、列表）可以读它的记录，权限和行级安全照旧；它永远不开放写，写仍只走动作自己的 `ai.exposed`。
- 为什么改：你在 #32442 裁定 A。今天 MCP 读工具按名字拒绝所有系统表，经理没法问 AI「我有哪些待审批」。本 PR 只做规格那一半（键的形状与规则）；让审批请求表真正可读的服务端那一半在 #32442。
- 风险与回滚：只是新增，旧元数据解析结果不变。业务对象上写这个键会在解析时被拒（它在业务对象上什么都不改，写 `false` 会让人误以为锁住了）；`sys_metadata`、`sys_metadata_history` 两张存元数据正文的表一律拒绝。运行时还没有任何地方读它。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/spec/src/data/ai-read-exposure.ts`（拒收与唯一读法 `isAiReadExposed`，元数据表先于键判断）；`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts` 中 `aiReadable` 键与写臂提示；`packages/spec/src/data/ai-read-exposure.test.ts`。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run src/data/ai-read-exposure.test.ts`，应见 17 个测试全绿。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

## What changes

`@objectstack/spec` gains a per-object, read-only AI exposure declaration, executing the maintainer's ruling A on the read half of #32442 (ruling record 6837430865).

- **`ObjectCapabilities.aiReadable`** (`enable.aiReadable`, optional boolean, absent by default). `true` declares that the AI read tools (query, get one, aggregate, describe, list) may reach this system object's records. Every gate after admission is unchanged: the caller's permissions, row-level security, field masking, and the object's API exposure. It never opens a write; a write on a system object stays on its actions, each opened by its own `ai.exposed` (ADR-0011). No deployment switch is added, and `allowSystemObjects` is untouched.
- **Parse refusal** in `ObjectSchema`'s existing refinement (`refuseMisplacedAiReadExposure` → `aiReadExposureRefusal`), so every door that parses an object inherits it (`ObjectSchema.create`, `defineStack`, `os validate`, the object save door):
  - the stored-metadata family is judged first. The list is `STORED_METADATA_BODY_OBJECTS` (`sys_metadata`, `sys_metadata_history`) in `packages/spec/src/kernel/stored-metadata-body-objects.ts`, the one list the action surface already refuses by (ADR-0066 D4, note of 2026-10-30). It is imported, not copied;
  - any object whose name does not start with `sys_` is refused: the MCP record tools already read a business object as the caller, so the key would change nothing there, and `false` would read as a lock that locks nothing (ADR-0049);
  - any declared value is judged, `false` included. The key is new, so no stored object carries it.
- **No write arm.** `enable` declares no other AI key. `aiExposed`, `aiWritable`, `aiWrite`, `aiEditable` and `ai` inside `enable` are refused with a read-only prescription that points writes at actions' `ai.exposed`; `aiRead`, `aiReadEnabled`, `aiReadExposed` and `mcpReadable` get a rename to `aiReadable`. A value that is not a boolean is refused.
- **`isAiReadExposed(schema)`**, exported from `@objectstack/spec/data`, is the one reading for the server half. It answers `false` for the stored-metadata family before it reads the key, `false` off a `sys_*` object, and `true` only for the boolean `true` (fail-closed, the shape of `isPublicSharingEnabled`).
- Liveness ledger: `object.enable.aiReadable` is `planned` until the server half lands. The Studio object form omits the key (reconciliation ledger row), because the objects that form edits are the ones the parse refuses it on.

### Placement and mechanism (measured; for the contract review)

- **`enable` rather than a new top-level `ai` block.** The MCP layer already reads an object's `enable` block for its record tools: `packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts` gates every data verb on `enable.apiEnabled` / `apiMethods`, and both bridges carry `enableFeatures: def.enable` into the object description (`packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts`). The new key sits beside the exposure flags it is read with, and `enable` already holds a read-only opt-in of the same kind (`approvalsVisibleToReaders`). A top-level `ai` block would add a second home for object exposure, and its `exposed` would read as full exposure.
- **The name.** `aiReadable` keeps the `ai` prefix and states the read-only scope in the name. The exact action spelling, `aiExposed`, is refused with guidance, because on an object it would read as write exposure too.
- **Parse instead of a `packages/lint` rule.** The card says the off-`sys_*` declaration is "refused by lint". A parse refusal is a strict superset: `os validate` reports parse issues, and the parse also covers `defineStack`, module load and the object save door, which a lint rule does not reach. This follows the precedents in the same refinement (`refuseWriteLockedUserActions`, `refuseExternalBindingOnPrimaryDatasource`). The claim's file surface was amended accordingly (claim re-post 6839889768). The contract review should confirm this mechanism change.

## Tests

`packages/spec/src/data/ai-read-exposure.test.ts`, 17 cases: accepted on `sys_approval_request` (true, false, absent); refused on a business object (true and false, located at `enable.aiReadable`); refused on each member of `STORED_METADATA_BODY_OBJECTS` (true and false); `isAiReadExposed` answers `false` on each family member **without reading the key** (getter probe, with a control leg on a non-family system object that is read); no write arm (`enable` declares exactly one `ai`/`mcp` key, the write-arm names are `unrecognized_keys`, non-boolean values are `invalid_type`, the reading opens on boolean `true` only).

Ablations (each rule once; `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` with an on-disk anchor proof, EXIT-trap restore, blob == HEAD verified after each; spec tests import `src/` directly, so no dist rebuild applies):

| Rule ablated | Result |
|:--|:--|
| A1 refusal off `sys_*` removed | 3 red (both business-object pins, the family-vs-business distinction) |
| A2 family refusal removed | 3 red (both family members, the distinction) |
| A3 family-before-key in `isAiReadExposed` removed | 2 red (both "without reading the key" pins) |
| A4 acceptance on `sys_*` removed | 1 red (the acceptance pin) |
| A5 a write-arm key added to `enable` | 1 red (the one-AI-key pin) |

Two existing tests were updated for the new key: `alias-integrity.test.ts` (the `enable` guidance table now lists the five write-arm names) and `metadata-form-zod-reconciliation.test.ts` (an `omit` ledger row for `object.enable.aiReadable`).

## Acceptance notes

- For the server half (#32442, carrier): the attestation should come from `isAiReadExposed` on the object's registered definition. Whether a tenant object overlay of a `sys_*` object can carry `enable.aiReadable` (ADR-0029 D9 overlays) is the server half's to measure; this PR measured only that an object extension cannot carry `enable` at all (`ObjectExtensionSchema` is closed and takes no `enable`).
- The three runtime copies of the `sys_` predicate (`packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts#isSystemObjectName`, and the module-private one here) are not unified; spec cannot import either runtime copy. Noted, not filed.
- After landing, the seat tells #32442's seat that its `Blocked-by:` edge has cleared; the merged key is `enable.aiReadable` and its reading is `isAiReadExposed`.
